written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385), the JOB statement's RESTART parameter (stepname, stepname.procstepname, *, checkid, the SYSCHK DD) and the EXEC statement's RD parameter, plus the COND / IF rules of slice 1. Written before any restart code ran on it. The manual's text was read by section through IBM's published z/OS 2.1 library (page numbers are not cited); the 2.1 wording was not re-read against the current release.
scenario_input: given: per step that starts in the restarted run, {rc: n}. Steps before the restart step have no entry (they do not execute).
scenario_answer: expect: per step, skipped (not executed because of the restart), run, or bypass (the COND / IF of the restart step or a later step kept it from starting).
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 4: JOB RESTART= (deferred step restart, procedure step,
//* RESTART=*, deferred checkpoint restart with SYSCHK, RD=). Answers in
//* scenarios.json, written from IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385
//* JOB RESTART) before any resolver ran.

scenarios.basis: RESTART=S3 without a checkid is a deferred step restart: the steps before S3 are not executed, S3 and every step after it are. S4's test (4,LT,S3) is false at rc 0.
The restart step and later steps keep their COND tests: S3 ends 8, so (4,LT,S3) is true and S4 is bypassed; S5's (0,NE) tests the steps executed so far (S3 only, A1), 8 NE 0 true, bypassed.
S5's bare COND=(0,NE) tests every preceding step that ran in this execution; the skipped steps have no return code this run (ASSUMED A1), so only S3 and S4 (both 0) are tested and S5 runs.
RESTART=* names the first step of the job: no step is skipped.
As a normal run: T3's (4,LT,T1) is true at rc 8.

RESTART=stepname.procstepname: stepname is the EXEC that calls the procedure, procstepname the procedure's step. Everything before CALL1.P2 (U0 and CALL1.P1) is skipped; P2, the rest of the procedure and the later job step run.
P3's COND=(4,LT,P2) names the restart step, which is allowed: rc 8 bypasses P3.

RESTART=(V3,CK1) with a SYSCHK DD before the first EXEC is a deferred checkpoint restart: V3 resumes at checkpoint CK1 (it still starts, and ends with a return code), the earlier steps are not executed, V4 runs.
RD=R on V3 governs automatic checkpoint restart after an abend of the running job; it does not change which steps a deferred restart runs.
The IF names the restart step W2, which ran in this execution: W2.RC = 0 is true, so the THEN clause (W3) runs.
W2.RC = 8 makes the IF false: the ELSE clause (W4) runs.

assumed.text: A step skipped by the restart has no return code in the restarted run, so a bare COND=(code,op) and a bare IF RC read only the steps that executed in it. IBM states the step-name referback restriction but not this; no real system's catalog of previous-run codes is consulted.

not_modelled: Automatic restart after a failure of the running job (RD=R / RNC, system restart): an action during a run, not a resubmission; the resolver reads JOB RESTART= only and does not read RD.

refused.construct: COND=(code,op,stepname) in the restart step or a later step naming a step before the restart step
refused.reason: IBM: the EXEC COND and PGM and the DD VOL=REF values naming a step that precedes the restart step must not be used in the restart step or later steps

refused.construct: RESTART=(step,checkid) with no SYSCHK DD before the first EXEC
refused.reason: IBM: a checkid needs a SYSCHK DD placed immediately before the first EXEC; without it the JCL is in error

refused.construct: RESTART= naming a step the job does not have
refused.reason: IBM: the system cannot restart at a step that is not in the job

refused.construct: an IF relational expression naming a step before the restart step
refused.reason: IBM's RESTART text lists COND, PGM and VOL=REF referbacks only; what an IF does with a skipped step is not stated, so it is refused rather than guessed

refused.construct: RESTART= naming the calling step of a procedure without a procstepname
refused.reason: IBM's syntax restarts at stepname.procstepname; the bare calling step is not stated
